questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid quoting a specific blockchain salary figure?
options: Specific numbers are illegal to discuss in a career-prep course
Salary figures go stale fast and vary by market, and this catalog has no reliable way to verify one as current -- so it teaches the research process instead
Salary negotiation is not relevant to blockchain engineering roles
Blockchain roles are never compensated with a salary of any kind
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly explains that it teaches a research process rather than quoting a number that could already be wrong or inapplicable to a reader's market.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what makes blockchain compensation research different from researching a typical tech role?
options: There is only one standard blockchain job title used industry-wide
Blockchain roles are always paid in cash with no other variation possible
Company stage has no effect on blockchain compensation
Unstandardized titles, wide swings by company stage, and token-based compensation as an added variable
questions.explain: The lesson names these three factors specifically as reasons blockchain pay varies even more than most tech roles.

questions.q: Per the lesson's negotiation principle, what happens when a candidate is the first to name a specific number in a salary conversation?
options: The conversation is required to end immediately
Naming a number first has no effect on the conversation
That number anchors the rest of the conversation
The employer is legally bound to that exact figure
questions.explain: The lesson states the same anchoring principle used elsewhere in this catalog: whoever names a number first shapes what follows.

questions.q: Besides the base salary, what else does the lesson say to evaluate in a real blockchain job offer?
options: The number of free snacks offered in the office
Any token grant and its vesting schedule, signing bonus, flexibility, and the timeline to the first compensation review
Nothing else matters beyond the base salary number
Only the company's total number of GitHub stars
questions.explain: The lesson lists token vesting, signing bonus, flexibility, and review timeline as real parts of total compensation to weigh.

questions.q: Which six courses does this lesson recap as making up the complete Blockchain Engineer path?
options: Three courses on Bitcoin and three unrelated courses on cloud computing

JavaScript & TypeScript for Blockchain Developers, Blockchain Development, Blockchain APIs & Backend Development, DeFi & Token Engineering, Blockchain Testing DevOps & Deployment, and Blockchain Engineering Capstones
Only this single capstones course, repeated six times
Six unrelated courses about general web development with no blockchain content
questions.explain: The lesson's recap names exactly these six courses, in order, as the complete path this final lesson closes out.
